narrative.overview: The whole site is a split-flap departures board seen in a concourse. Real figures fall into fixed character cells letter by letter, the board is always matte black with painted white lettering, and everything around it is steel: light, flat steel by day, a dark hall by night. The board is not a picture of a board; it is the working interface, a semantic table whose cells happen to be flaps, with the real text always available underneath. Density is the board's: fixed columns, ranked rows, tabular numerals, and nothing decorative between them. Colour is almost absent on purpose, so that the two signal inks mean exactly one thing each.
keyCharacteristics: Four inks only: flap black, paint white, lamp amber (late or changing now), cancel red (cancelled).
Condensed uppercase lettering in fixed cells; system UI type for reading.
Flat steel frames around every board; no imitated textures.
One credited photograph per surface at most, framed like a concourse poster.
Motion is the flap: a character-by-character cascade, reduced to a direct swap when the system asks for less motion.

rules.name: The One Meaning Rule
rules.body: Amber means late, changing or "act here"; red means cancelled. If a third meaning appears, it gets neither colour.

rules.name: The Ink Data Rule
rules.body: Chart series are drawn in ink (flap black by day, paint white by night) on steel plates; sequential ramps run from the plate tone to the ink. Status colours never paint a data series.

rules.name: The Cell Rule
rules.body: Announced text lives in fixed cells: a value that does not fit is shortened at a word boundary, the way real boards abbreviate, never cut mid-word.

rules.name: The Frame Rule
rules.body: Only framed boards and the primary button cast shadows; plates and controls are flat.

dos: Do put lists of departures, steps and figures in fixed flap cells inside a steel-framed black board.
Do keep amber (#f2a900) for delays, the board clock and the primary action, and red (#c8372d) for cancellations only.
Do draw chart data in ink on steel plates, with sequential ramps from plate tone to ink.
Do credit every photograph next to it (author, licence, source) and embed its origin in the file.
Do keep the real text of every flap available to assistive technology and honour prefers-reduced-motion.
donts: Don't imitate materials in CSS (pinstripe "brushed steel", fake grain); steel is flat tone.
Don't use AENA or airline branding, logos or liveries; this is an independent project.
Don't add more than one photograph per surface, or photographs without a clear role.
Don't use emoji or Unicode glyphs as icons; icons are Lucide line icons.
Don't set announced text in the system face, or reading text in the condensed face.
